purpose: Train and adversarially challenge DayTrade Lens. Evidence is educational/research input, not a live trading recommendation.

lessons.title: Skill must beat the base rate, not just a backtest

sources.note: Taiwan 1992-2006; aggregate net performance negative in every studied year, vast majority unprofitable, with a small skilled minority reported in related work.
Emphasizes severe loss risk, expenses, leverage risk, and skepticism toward easy-profit claims.

lessons.principle: A research program must assume skill is rare until prospective evidence proves otherwise.
attacks: Report base-rate-adjusted evidence, not only conditional survivor performance.
Track every attempted signal family and dead candidate so failures cannot disappear.
Require prospective sample readiness before any performance claim.

lessons.title: The search process is part of the hypothesis

sources.authority: Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado, Zhu
sources.note: Introduces probability of backtest overfitting and warns that ordinary holdouts can be unreliable after strategy selection.

lessons.principle: The more variants we inspect, the less impressive the winner should look.
attacks: Preserve a complete trial ledger across instruments, horizons, benchmarks, delays and filters.
Estimate family-level multiple-testing burden and probability of backtest overfitting where the data support it.
Use walk-forward/purged folds and never retune frozen prospective protocols from later outcomes.

lessons.title: A Sharpe-like statistic is meaningless without its search history

sources.note: Deflated Sharpe Ratio adjusts performance claims for multiple testing and non-normal returns.

lessons.principle: Performance statistics must be deflated by trials, skew, kurtosis and finite sample uncertainty.
attacks: Add DSR/PBO-style diagnostics only as exploratory historical evidence unless predeclared.
Record skew, kurtosis and downside tails rather than mean return alone.
Penalize strategy families for the full number of research configurations actually attempted.

lessons.title: Paper alpha is not executable alpha

sources.note: Explicit and implicit costs include spread, market impact, delay and unfilled-trade opportunity costs.
Implementation shortfall decomposes delay, execution and opportunity costs and is a standard trade-cost measure.

lessons.principle: Entry, fill probability, spread, delay, opportunity cost and exit mechanics belong inside the edge definition.
attacks: Score implementation shortfall from decision timestamp to simulated fills.
Separate signal decay from execution cost.
Model unfilled or partially filled orders as outcomes, never silently as perfect fills.

lessons.title: Execution is a risk-cost frontier

sources.note: Models the tradeoff between volatility risk and temporary/permanent market impact.

lessons.principle: There is no universal best entry speed; urgency changes impact cost and exposure to price risk.
attacks: Stress multiple execution speeds and participation assumptions.
Report fill-path risk and maximum adverse excursion alongside terminal return.
Treat tiny-capital execution as an empirical plumbing test rather than a scale-free proof of profitability.

lessons.title: The book is information, not scenery

sources.authority: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.note: Finds both trades and limit orders affect price dynamics, with announcement periods increasing price impact.

lessons.principle: A price-only backtest can miss the state variable that determines whether the signal is tradable.
attacks: When data become available, test spread, depth, imbalance and order-flow state at event time.
Do not infer liquidity from volume alone.
Compare aggressive and passive execution assumptions rather than one universal fill rule.

lessons.title: Public information creates a changing microstructure regime

sources.authority: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.note: Around major announcements, volatility can jump before trading volume, while spreads widen and later narrow as trading increases.

lessons.principle: The first tradable minutes after news can have radically different spread, depth and adverse-selection conditions from normal time.
attacks: Condition execution stress on announcement proximity and volatility state.
Measure delay sensitivity beyond 5/15/30 minutes and next-session open.
Do not treat the first available bar as equivalent to a realistically obtainable fill.

lessons.title: Clock time is market structure

sources.note: Opening Cross occurs at 9:30 ET, with imbalance dissemination beginning at 9:25; distinct auction order types and mechanics apply.

lessons.principle: Open, continuous session and close are different mechanisms; a timestamp is not just another row.
attacks: Separate opening-auction, immediate-post-open, continuous-session and next-open entries.
Flag events whose modeled public time lands near auction/imbalance windows.
Never use continuous-market fill assumptions for auction timestamps without explicit modeling.

lessons.title: Volume is not liquidity

sources.authority: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.note: Bid-ask spread and price impact are stronger liquidity measures than trading volume/frequency, which can be poor proxies.

lessons.principle: A strategy can look liquid by volume while being expensive in spread or price impact.
attacks: Measure spread, depth and impact separately whenever available.
Add missing-liquidity-data state instead of substituting volume.
Stress the edge in low-depth/high-volatility regimes.

lessons.title: Familiarity can masquerade as information

sources.note: Documents familiarity bias in day trading and argues top-of-mind dominance can explain it.

lessons.principle: A compelling narrative can increase attention without increasing predictive information.
attacks: Create narrative-blind controls that preserve timestamp/issuer structure while hiding the story label.
Test whether branded themes such as AI outperform matched non-theme filings after identical selection rules.
Require evidence that the semantic label adds information beyond earnings, macro timing and market regime.
